products.dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on both flags, but it took the photo to see why. assets/products/revelate-designs/cranny-cranny-frame-back-black (local copy cranny-cranny-frame-bag-0-6l-1.jpg) shows a small CRESCENT-shaped wedge with three velcro tabs -- fat and rounded where it meets the head-tube corner and tapering away to nothing along both edges. Its outline fills well under half its own bounding box, and the 9.5 cm width is the MAXIMUM at the fat end, not a uniform thickness. That is the whole explanation for the volume-too-big flag (box 3.6 L against 0.6 L): integrate a wedge that tapers from 9.5 cm to zero over a crescent outline and you land at roughly 0.6-0.7 L. Revelate quotes 38 cu in (0.62 L) and 72 g -- a 72 g bag is not a 3.6 L box. The too-cubic flag fails for the same reason: a corner wedge is not a top-tube sliver and cannot be 2.2:1. All three axes are bike-packing.de's as printed. Revelate blocks bots, so this figure is retailer-sourced (dims_source: retailer) and is weaker evidence than a maker spec block.

products.dims_raw: Dimensions: 233 x 108 x 127 x 51mm (9.2 x 4.3 x 5 x 2"); Capacity: 0.7 liter; Weight: 130g / 4.6oz
products.dims_note: REAL ERROR on capacity, small correction on dims. Blackburn quotes FOUR numbers because the bag is a wedge that sits in the corner behind the head tube: 233mm long, two heights of 108 and 127mm, and 51mm wide. hgt is the taller of the two heights. The catalogue also carried 1.5L against Blackburn's published 0.7L - more than double - which is what made the shape flag look worse than it was. 23.3 x 12.7 x 5.1 = 1.51L bounding box against 0.7L, exactly right for a triangular wedge that fills about half its box.

products.dims_note: DUPLICATED AXIS - the defect the brief warned about. The record held len 35 and hgt 35, the same number twice, plus wid 14 and dia 14, and 4L. Blackburn publishes '6.5 liters at 325mm (3 rolls) x 150mm': it is a plain cylindrical roll-top dry bag strapped into a fork or frame cargo cage, so there is only a length and a diameter. Corrected to a 32.5cm cylinder of 15cm diameter, giving 7.3L of box against the published 6.5L (ratio 1.12) where the old figures gave 17.1L against 4L (ratio 4.29). products.name: Local Plus Top Tube Bag

products.dims_note: REAL ERROR, now maker-sourced. The record had no source at all (dims_source none) and carried 19 x 11 x 8, which is too short and too tall. Blackburn publishes 76 x 89 x 203mm: 203 is unambiguously the length, and of the remaining pair 89 is the height and 76 the width, the usual proportion for a phone-over-the-top-tube bag. The correction also clears the flag on its own - 20.3/8.9 = 2.28 now passes the 2.0 elongation rule where the stored figures gave 1.73. 20.3 x 8.9 x 7.6 = 1.37L against the stated 1L.

products.dims_note: CORRECTED, low confidence. Rockgeist's own two numbers cannot both be true: a 26.7 x 7.6cm oval base 15.2cm tall is 3.1L against a rated 9-10L, and no drawstring sleeve closes a 3x gap. The studio photo on a Jones Loop bar (dr-jones-dr-jones-bag-one-size-1.webp) settles the shape - it is a deep, near-cubic box roughly 30cm across the front face and about 19-20cm tall, with a narrow structured base that flares outward, not a slim 3in-deep pouch; bikepacking.com's launch piece calls it 'a deep bag'. Kept the maker's 10.5in (26.7cm) bar-width; reconstructed height 20cm and depth 15cm so the box lands on the 8L that bikepacking.com's launch spec states (its 282g weight matches Rockgeist's 283g, so it is the same product data). Rockgeist's '6" tall / 3" oval' describes the collapsed structured shell only. Capacity moved 10 -> 8 to the launch figure.

Both mounted photos (microwave-...-3.jpg rear view, -4.jpg on trail) show the grey dry bag sitting well proud of the black holster and bulging past its 4in depth once loaded. Checking the dry bag: a 22 x 13.5in flat panel is a 21.8cm-diameter tube about 16L unrolled, so 13L is reached at roughly 35cm of packed height - consistent with a 30.5cm holster plus around 10cm of bag standing above it. Set the as-mounted box to 25.4 fore/aft (holster width, unchanged) x 40 tall x 14 across, 14.2L, a 1.09 fill on 13L. Height and width are reconstructed from the dry bag geometry plus the photos, not published.

products.name: Rollpacker Rear 20L
products.dims_raw: Closed width: 38 cm (15"); Open width: 46.5 cm (18.3"); Height of main compartment: 9" (24 cm); Depth excluding front pocket: 28 cm; Depth including front pocket: 13.5" (43.3 cm); 20L (1220.5 cu. in.) plus a 2L front pocket
products.dims_note: TRANSPOSED AXES. The record had no source and read len 38 / wid 28. Arkel's published figures are 'closed width 38 cm' and 'depth excluding front pocket 28 cm', and for a seat pack len is the fore-aft dimension, so those two were the wrong way round: len = 28 (depth), wid = 38 (across-bike width). hgt 24 was already Arkel's 'height of main compartment' and is unchanged. The elongation rule still fails at 1.36 and that is a genuine shape, not an error - the Rollpacker is Arkel's unusually wide box-shaped rear bag carried on its own rigid rack, not a tapered saddle tube. 28 x 24 x 38 = 25.5L against a rated 20L (ratio 1.28). ROLL RANGE: Arkel give 'closed width 38 cm / open width 46.5 cm'; wid uses the CLOSED end per the closed-end rule, so this record is already compliant - do not swap it to 46.5. (The other Arkel range, depth 28cm excluding vs 43.3cm including the front pocket, is a with/without-pocket figure rather than a roll, and 28cm is the one that matches the 20L main-compartment rating; the front pocket is rated separately at 2L.)

products.name: Arkel GT-54 Classic Touring Panniers
products.dims_raw: Arkel spec: 'Volume: 54 L (3300 cu. in.)'; listing title 'GT-54 Classic Touring Panniers (Pair)'; scope of delivery one left and one right pannier
products.dims_note: PAIR/SINGLE MISMATCH, not a dimension error. The 54L is Arkel's PAIR total - the listing ships a left and a right bag and Arkel names the model after the combined volume, exactly as it does with the Dolphin (24L each, 48L per pair). The stored dims are per-bag, so the checker was comparing one bag's box against two bags' capacity. Per bag the reconciliation is fine: 33.7 x 36.2 x 20 = 24.4L against 27L (ratio 0.90), the remainder taken up by the expanding outer pockets and the drawstring collar. Dims unchanged; litres corrected to the per-bag figure.

products.name: Dolphin 24L
products.dims_raw: Arkel spec: 'Total Volume (per bag): 24L'; sold as a single pannier ($179.99) or as a pair ($339.99)
products.dims_note: PAIR/SINGLE MISMATCH, same defect as the GT-54. The product is named 'Dolphin 24L' and Arkel states 24L PER BAG, but the record carried 48 - the pair total - while the dims were for one bag. Arkel's page confirms both a single and a pair purchase option. The dims are right and need no change: 33 x 48 x 15 = 23.8L against 24L per bag, a 0.99 reconciliation. On the closed-end rule: Arkel publish NO height range for the Dolphin, only the single 24L per-bag rating, and the stored 48cm is the one height that reproduces it, so there is no range to take the closed end of and the rule does not bite here. If a range does surface later this is the record to revisit, since a rolled-down Dolphin is certainly shorter than 48cm.

WOHO labels the axes L x W x H but their 'W' is the vertical drop and their 'H' the across-bike thickness, so the catalogue's len/hgt/wid mapping is already correct. Same class as the Apidura and Ripio full-frame flags from chunk 1: a bag shaped to a main triangle cannot reach 1.5:1. Box 14.4 L against 12 L is 1.20x -- if anything this is one of the better-reconciled records in the batch. Dims upgraded from unknown to maker-sourced; nothing changed.

products.name: XTouring UL Pannier Dry
products.dims_raw: Bikerumor (from WOHO): "Size: 28cm to 49cm tall (depending on roll top), 32cm wide, and 13cm deep. Volume: 36 liters a pair (roll top fully open), 20 liters a pair (rolled three times). Weight: 350g (single), 700g (pair)". BIKEPACKING.com launch: "49cm (full)-35 (rolled 3 times) tall x 32cm wide x 13cm deep"
products.dims_note: CORRECTED -- the stored 40 x 24 x 14 matched no published axis on this bag and looks back-computed. Two independent press sources working from WOHO's own release agree: 32 cm wide (fore-aft on the rack), 13 cm deep (across the bike), and 28-49 cm tall depending on how far the roll-top is closed, with 35 cm being rolled three times. Recorded as the packed, as-mounted state: len 32, hgt 35, wid 13. On the volume-too-small flag the answer is THE LITRES ARE THE MAXIMUM-ROLL FIGURE: 36 L a pair fully open = 18 L per bag is the catalogue's number and is correct per bag, but it belongs to the 49 cm fully-open height (32 x 49 x 13 = 20.4 L, ratio 1.13). Rolled three times the bag is 14.6 L. capacity_l left at 18 per bag. One outlier noted and rejected: thecyclelist.co lists 8.25 x 5 x 19.25 in (21 x 12.7 x 48.9 cm), agreeing on the 13 cm depth and the 49 cm height but giving 21 cm where both press sources say 32 cm; a 21 cm-wide 18 L pannier is not credible. WOHO's own product URL for this model 404s, so this is press-sourced, not maker-page-sourced.

products.name: Transporter MIK Pannier Bag 30L
products.dims_raw: Giant: "Size: 30*17*40cm", "Weight: 1400g", "Volume: 30L"; multiple Giant dealers print "Volume: 30L (15L per side)"
products.dims_note: CORRECTED on two counts, and the photo drove both. assets/products/giant/transporter-transporter-mik-pannier-bag-30l-30l-single-1.jpg and -2.jpg show a DOUBLE pannier -- two bags joined by a saddle panel that drapes over the rack -- and each half is clearly PORTRAIT, measurably about 1.45x taller than it is long. (1) AXIS ORDER. Giant's page gives a bare '30*17*40cm' with no labels, and the catalogue had read the 40 as fore-aft depth, which would make each bag landscape -- the opposite of the photo. Remapped to len 30 (fore-aft along the rack), hgt 40 (vertical), wid 17 (across the bike). 40/30 = 1.33 against the ~1.45 measured off the photo, the difference being the roll top standing proud. A 40 cm fore-aft pannier would also foul the rider's heel; 30 x 40 x 17 is the standard commuter-pannier envelope (cf. Ortlieb Back-Roller at 32 x 42 x 17). (2) CAPACITY. The 30 L is the PAIR, not one bag. Giant dealers print 'Volume: 30L (15L per side)'; MIK ('Mounting Is Key') is a top-of-rack plate system, so a MIK pannier bag is necessarily a two-sided unit rather than a single hanging bag; and 1400 g is a double-bag weight. The catalogue models one side in the pannier slot, so capacity_l is set to 15. That also clears the volume-too-small flag: the per-side box is 20.4 L against 15 L per side, a ratio of 1.36, textbook for a roll-top. Note the size string still reads '30L (single)' and is misleading, but it is the join key so it is left alone.

products.name: Handlebar Bag ADV
products.dims_raw: Capacity: 19L. Dimensions: length 22cm/8.5" (when the roll top is stretched: 38cm/15"), width 42cm/16.5" (including side pockets), depth 22cm/8.5". Material: Cordura Nylon Fabric
products.dims_note: DIMS ARE RIGHT, THE SLOT IS WRONG. The photos settle it: assets/products/fairweather/handlebar-bag-handlebar-bag-adv-one-size-19l-1.jpg shows a structured, squared-off rando/porteur box sitting on a front rack with lidded side pockets and a MOLLE-webbed front panel, and -2.jpg shows the strap-to-bar mounting close up. It is not a drybag roll. Every other barroll in this catalogue is a cylinder 40-65 cm long and 15-20 cm in diameter (Sweetroll, Ortlieb Handlebar-Pack, Tailfin, WOHO); a 42 x 26.8 x 22 box is not in that family, which is precisely why the 1.8 elongation check fired at 1.57. Reclassified to barbag, where its nearest neighbour is the Swift Zeitgeist (48.3 x 22.9 x 17.8, 12 L). Dimensions themselves check out against the photo: measuring image 1, total width including side pockets is ~1.6x the body height, matching 42 vs 26.8. Box 24.8 L against a rated 19 L (1.3x), normal for a rolltop measured part-extended. Bluelug's 'length' is the vertical roll dimension (22 cm down, 38 cm stretched), which is why hgt sits between the two.

products.name: Frame Bag ADV (Medium)
products.dims_raw: Size small - Capacity: 3.6 liters, Dimension: L 33cm x H 27.5cm x W 6cm. Size medium - Capacity: 4L, Dimension: L 34cm x H 33cm x W 6cm. Weight: 141g (AVG.)
products.dims_note: FALSE POSITIVE on BOTH flags, settled by the two photos. assets/products/fairweather/frame-bag-frame-bag-adv-medium-medium-4l-1.jpg (teal, on a bike) and -2.jpg (coyote, on a green MTB) both show a near-equilateral TRIANGLE hanging from the top tube -- measuring image 1, the bag's top edge and its vertical extent are the same length to within a few percent, which is 34 x 33 exactly as bluelug prints it. (1) too-cubic: the 2.2 elongation rule assumes a framebag_half is a long sliver under the top tube; this one is a full-height front-corner triangle, so 1.03 is the true shape, not a transposition. (2) too-big-for-frame at 33 cm: the photos ARE the disproof -- the bag is mounted on real bikes with a bottle cage still usable below it. A 56cm gravel main triangle is ~45 cm tall at the seat tube, so 33 cm fits with room to spare; the 30 cm cap is too tight. Volume reconciles on the correct triangular basis: 34 x 33 x 6 / 2 = 3.4 L against a rated 4 L, with the bulge making up the difference. Fixed-size zip bag, so L x H x W maps straight across.

features.mount: multiple strap loops so one bag fits a range of frame sizes
